newsitem.title: USA: Worldwide PC market grew 16 percent in 1996 - IDC.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide PC market grew 16 percent in 1996 - IDC.

text.p: Growth in U.S. and worldwide personal computer markets slowed to the lowest rates in years during 1996, International Data Corp. said Monday.
The technology research firm said worldwide unit shipments rose 16 percent from 1995, marking the first year since 1991 in which sales did not increase by at least 20 percent.
According to preliminary year-end data, IDC said U.S. shipments rose 15 percent, following a very strong 1995.
It said the fourth quarter was weak worldwide, growing only 11 percent, due mainly to depressed sales in Europe.

Compaq Computer Corp. maintained its lead in both the U.S. and global markets for the third year, fending off a challenge from International Business Machines Corp., which gained market share for the first time since 1993.
Apple Computer Inc. lost market share, while Hewlett-Packard Co. made its maiden appearance on the list of the top five PC vendors worldwide.
